thread:
Sam K.: Quick sync — I started a pass over our internal incident comms templates. Want to tighten placeholders and tone so on-call can grab and send without edits. Thoughts?

Anita Varela: +1. We still have too many variants floating around. Would help to standardize sections and a short/long pair for status page + customer email.

Lee Park: Agreed. Also want a concise handoff snippet the on-call can paste into PagerDuty notes. Keep it short: impact, current mitigation, next action, ETA.

online incident-bot: "Handoff created: Incident 1795009876 - paging: oncall-eng. Current assignee: Lee Park." 

Maria G.: Can we add clear placeholder names (not freeform) so reviewers know what to fill? Eg: {{service}}, {{impact_summary}}, {{mitigation_steps}}, {{eta_local}}.

Priya (Ops Lead): Please include two tone presets: "neutral" (for in-progress updates) and "empathic" (for customer-facing postmortems). Neutral = factual, concise; Empathic = acknowledgement + remediation + compensation next steps (if needed).

Sam K.: Here's a draft minimal template (for internal incident thread and quick handoff):

```
[Incident {{incident_id}}] - {{service}} - {{severity}}
Impact: {{impact_summary}}
Started: {{start_utc}}
Current status: {{current_status}}
Mitigation in progress: {{mitigation_steps}}
Next action & owner: {{next_action}} - {{owner_handle}}
ETA for next update: {{eta_local}}
Docs/links: {{runbook_link}}, {{dashboard_link}}
```

Lee Park: This is good. Add a one-line TL;DR at the top for status page use: "TL;DR: {{one_line}}" so the status engineer can copy it directly.

Sam K.: Good call. Also adding a customer-facing short blurb (neutral tone) — ~2 sentences: 

```
We are currently investigating an issue affecting {{service}} which may cause {{user_visible_impact}}. Our team is actively working on a fix and we will post updates by {{eta_local}}.
```

Maria G.: Suggest an empathic variant for email: 

```
We apologize for the disruption to {{service}}. Between {{start_local}} and {{end_local_or_present}} some customers experienced {{user_visible_impact}}. We have implemented {{mitigation_summary}} and are monitoring for normal behavior. If you continue to see issues, please contact support at {{support_contact}}.
```

Priya (Ops Lead): Make sure to include a short internal-only section for impact assessment: estimated % of requests affected, critical customers impacted, and any outage window. That helps triage comms escalation.

Julian H.: Also we need a checkbox list for the on-call handoff message so the next person can confirm steps quickly. Something like:

- [ ] Confirm mitigation applied
- [ ] Restarted affected services (if applicable)
- [ ] Run verification tests (link)
- [ ] Notify customers on status page

Sam K.: I'm going to add a small style guide: preferred phrasing (avoid words like "catastrophic"), prefer UTC timestamps then local in parentheses, and always include links. Also we should provide a short list of fallback phrases for unknown ETA: "investigating", "mitigation underway", "targeting next update in ~15m".

Anita Varela: Can we include a pre-approved legal-friendly line for potential data integrity incidents? Something ops can copy verbatim to avoid slow approvals.

Sam K.: Good point. Draft legal-safe line: "We are investigating reports of potential data inconsistencies. At this time, there is no evidence of data exfiltration. We will provide a full report once we have completed our investigation." (flagged for security/legal review before shipping into templates).

incident-bot: "Reminder: After the incident, run the postmortem checklist: create timeline, collect logs (s3://incidents/{{incident_id}}/logs), attach comms used, and tag impacted customers."

Maria G.: Next steps: Sam to open a repo PR with templates + examples; Priya to review tone presets; Legal to sign off on the data line. Can we aim for a small rollout to the on-call team by EOD tomorrow?

Priya (Ops Lead): I can review tomorrow morning. If Sam posts the PR tonight I'll get at it first thing.

Lee Park: I'll convert the handoff snippet into a PagerDuty note template so it's one-click for on-call.

Sam K.: Thanks all. I'll create: 1) one-line TL;DR template, 2) internal handoff checklist, 3) 2 customer-facing tone variants, 4) legal-safe lines (flagged). PR link will be posted here when ready.

Julian H.: FYI: if anyone wants to test copywriting quickly, we have a small set of real incident prompts in "#devex-writing-practice" — useful to see how concise comms read under time pressure.

Sam K.: PR posted: https://git.internal.redwood/repo/incidents-templates/pull/42 (will ping once ready for review).

Anita Varela: Great work. Small ask — add a short example status page timeline (3 bullets) so support can paste into status page updates without hunting log links.

Sam K.: Will do. I'll include sample timelines and a short decision matrix for when to escalate to CS and when to issue a customer email.

Maria G.: Thanks team. This should cut down time to first-update and make handoffs less noisy.

Priya (Ops Lead): Closing loop: once legal okays the line, Ops will push templates to the runbook and notify on-call rotation.
